findings.problem: On the phone, the first press of a stepper makes the whole editor jump 64px up the screen, and the band it vacates is filled with a half a row. Measured at 390x844 on paper AND ink, owner-flight/owner-editing: at rest .b-edit is fixed with bottom:12px (rect 294..832); on the first +7 press b.css:1394 ([data-undo="true"][data-editor-open] .b-edit { bottom: 76px; }) fires and the sheet snaps to 230..768 - no transition, so the +7 button itself translates 64px out from under the thumb (.b-step y 526 -> 462 at 390; 706 -> 642 at 768; 482 -> 418 at 1023; identical on both grounds). Nothing is ever painted in the 64px it gives up: moveUndoBar (render-b.js:1091) relocates the single .b-undo INTO .b-edit whenever the editor is open, and .b-undoHome measures 0 children / 0px height at that moment, so the rule reserves a band for a bar that is sitting inside the sheet. What actually shows through the strip is a live moment cut in half by the sheet's own rounded bottom edge - at 390 that is the Wedding day row (top 757, sheet bottom 768), the plan's terminus, sliced across its cap-height. The gate's own 'the steppers do not move under the pointer' is proven only at 1440x960 (interaction-check.mjs:332), the one width where .b-edit is position:relative and this cannot happen. This is the product's signature gesture, on the screen the owner will actually use, and it flinches.
findings.fix: Delete b.css:1394 ([data-undo="true"][data-editor-open] .b-edit { bottom: 76px; }). The band it reserves is only ever occupied when the editor is CLOSED - verified: on Escape the bar moves to .b-undoHome and becomes position:fixed at 755..832 - and the closed case is already handled by the [data-undo="true"] .b-undoHome .b-undo rule at b.css:1386 plus the padding/scroll-padding reserve at 1377-1385. With it gone the sheet holds bottom:12px through the move, the steppers stay under the finger, and no row is bisected. Then widen interaction-check.mjs's primary-gesture block (line 332) from the single 1440x960 viewport to [{390,844},{768,1024},{1440,960}] so 'the steppers do not move under the pointer' and 'the page keeps its place through the move' are proven on the docked editor as well as the desk one.

findings.element: .b-live on the publish screen, driven path only
findings.problem: The owner's last act - pressing Publish and handing the day over - ends on a sentence that is painted in the composition and is spatially false. go() (render-b.js:1450) writes SAID.publish into .b-live, and the publish screen's .b-live (render-b.js:1805) carries NO .b-vh, unlike the two owner-shell copies at 1475 and 1536. Measured at 390x844 after pressing Publish, identical on paper and ink: .b-live renders at y 899..919, 13px, color var(--fore) - full ink density, DARKER than the .b-note beneath it at fore-62 - reading 'Ready to send. The link is below.' from a draft, or just 'The link is below.' from a live plan. The link field it points at sits at 752..819 and the Copy control at 848..887: the link is 147px ABOVE the line that says it is below. So the foot of the most important screen in the owner's flow reads 'Copy the link / SENDING COMES NEXT / The link is below. / You can turn the link off at any time...' - four words of the highest-contrast text on the block, describing a direction that does not exist. It survived nine rounds because it only exists on the driven path: ?state=publish loads with .b-live empty, so every frame ever reviewed is clean, and round 8's refuter called it 'the announced strap' on the assumption it was never painted.
findings.fix: Separate the arrival announcement from the visible status line. In render-b.js, insert h("p.b-liveNav.b-vh", { role: "status", text: "" }) immediately after the .b-who 'THE LINK' node in the press block, and in go() (line 1450) change var live = document.querySelector(".b-live") to var live = document.querySelector(".b-liveNav") || document.querySelector(".b-live"). The visible .b-live then stays empty on arrival and is only ever filled by the copy handler ('Copied.' / 'Copy did not work. Select the link and copy it by hand.'), which is what it was drawn for. Then strip the spatial clause from SAID.publish (render-b.js:1430) - return F_PUBLISHED() ? "The plan is live." : "Ready to send." - because an announcement read aloud on arrival should name the state, not a direction on a page its listener cannot see.

biggestWin: The measure is drawn to scale, and that one decision is the whole product's feeling. Sixteen days between today and the menu tasting is 193px of blank paper you have to push past with your thumb (12.05px per day, constant, phone / desk / A4 alike), and the gap note names the void instead of apologising for it - 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' No other planning tool makes you feel a fortnight. The single memorable moment is what that build pays for on the morning: the whole counting apparatus - the 79, the rail, the days-away column - is gone, and the screen is MARA & FINN / Today / Saturday 3 October 2026 / a hairline / 'This is the day the plan was for.' The number that ran the product for months resolves into one word, centred, at 75px, and the only indigo left on the page is the rule above 'HAPPENING NOW'. That is a real ending, not a state, and it is the reason I would believe a top studio made this.
